body:
DebianPrep is a lightweight automation script designed to simplify the process of configuring new Debian-based servers. Whether you’re setting up a local virtual machine or connecting to a remote VPS, DebianPrep helps you get a clean, ready-to-code environment in minutes.

Definition: DebianPrep automates the installation of essential tools, utilities, and system configurations that are commonly needed right after deploying a fresh Debian or Ubuntu server.

🚀 Purpose

When you spin up a new server, you often repeat the same initial setup tasks: updating packages, installing common utilities, configuring firewalls, enabling SSH, and more. DebianPrep automates all these actions through a single command.

🖥️ Supported Systems

DebianPrep supports all Debian-based Linux distributions, including:

  • Ubuntu (20.04 and newer)
  • Debian (10 and newer)
  • Linux Mint
  • Pop!_OS and more

⚙️ Features

  • Automatic package updates and upgrades
  • Installs essential tools: curl, wget, git, ufw, htop
  • Sets up SSH and basic firewall rules
  • Creates a system cleanup and optimization routine
  • Fast and idempotent; safe to run multiple times

📦 Installation

To run DebianPrep, simply execute the following command after connecting to your new Debian-based server:

bash
curl -L -o debianprep https://github.com/doe-base/debianprep/releases/download/v1.0.0/debianprep
chmod +x debianprep
./debianprep

This will download the script from the official GitHub repository and execute it immediately.

🧰 What It Installs

CategoryTools
Networkingcurl, wget, net-tools, openssh-server
System Utilitieshtop, unzip, tar, ufw, git
Developmentbuild-essential, pkg-config, make

🔧 Usage

DebianPrep can be used on any fresh Debian-based system. Run it immediately after gaining SSH access:

bash
ssh user@your-server-ip
curl -L -o debianprep https://github.com/doe-base/debianprep/releases/download/v1.0.0/debianprep
chmod +x debianprep
sudo mv debianprep /usr/local/bin/
debianprep

The script handles everything automatically. Once complete, your environment will be updated and ready for use.

🧠 Behind the Scenes

DebianPrep is written in Go and structured using modular internal commands for maintainability. Each command handles a distinct setup area; such as user creation, package installation, and security configuration.

📘 License

DebianPrep is released under the MIT License. Feel free to modify and reuse it for your own setup workflows.

🔗 Reference

Net Reader is a decentralized local web application built with Go and React. It enables devices on the same Local Area Network (LAN) to discover peers, inspect network configurations, communicate directly, and access remote filesystems—without relying on a central server.

🎯 Purpose & Goals

Net Reader was created to make LAN networking visible and observable rather than hiding it behind high-level abstractions. It demonstrates core networking concepts—such as IP addressing, UDP broadcasting, TCP sockets, and peer presence tracking—in an accessible interface.

🖥️ Platform Architecture

  • Frontend: React UI (Dashboard, Chat, Filesystem)
  • Backend: Go Server (Network inspection, UDP/TCP sockets, Local API, Event Log)
  • Network Scope: Local Area Network (LAN)
  • Model: Decentralized Peer-to-Peer

📡 How Discovery Works

Every device running Net Reader continuously broadcasts its identity (Host name, IP) over UDP broadcast and listens for packets from other peers. 

1. App Starts -> Inspect local interfaces & IPs
2. Listen for UDP broadcast packets on port
3. Broadcast local identity packet to LAN
4. On packet received:
   ├── Same IP (Self)  ➔ Filter/Ignore
   └── New/Known IP   ➔ Update peer table & LastSeen timestamp

Peers update their LastSeen timestamp upon receiving repeated broadcasts. If a peer stops broadcasting past an expiry threshold, it is automatically removed from the active list.

🔌 Communication & Protocols

Net Reader separates discovery from direct peer interaction using distinct protocols for distinct tasks:

Protocol Purpose
UDP Broadcast Lightweight, continuous peer presence & identity broadcast
TCP Sockets Reliable peer connections (1:1 messaging, filesystem access)
HTTP / Local API Communication between React browser UI and local Go backend

⚙️ Key Features

  • Network Inspection: Real-time display of local IP, MAC address, host machine name, and network interface.
  • Peer Discovery: Automatic network discovery via UDP with self-filtering and lifetime presence management.
  • Peer Messaging: Send targeted private messages (TCP) or LAN-wide broadcast messages.
  • Filesystem Access: Request and browse file structures directly from discovered peers.
  • Event Timeline: Live log tracking network events (e.g., PEER_DISCOVERED, CONNECTION_ESTABLISHED, PEER_EXPIRED).

🔭 Future Direction

  • Interactive visual network topology map
  • Direct file transfer progress indicators
  • Multi-interface selection and binding
  • Cross-platform performance improvements

License: Released under the MIT License.
Source Code: GitHub Repository
